reproduction_target: Oxford Nanopore long-read genomic DNA and direct-RNA characterisation of CRISPR-engineered FSHD myoblast/myotube lines (DEL9_SM double mutant) versus the isogenic parental control. The computational reproduction target is the analysis half of the study: Dogme v1.2.2 nextflow processing (dorado basecalling, minimap2 mapping, samtools, modkit modification extraction, LR-kallisto/bustools quantification) against GRCh38 and CHM13 T2T, DSS differentially-methylated-site calling, promoter-region construction from a GENCODE annotation by a custom script, region-level methylation scoring with modkit dmr pair plus UCSC RepeatMasker/mappability tracks, Clair3 variant calling and WhatsHap read phasing, reconcileBams.py novel-isoform reconciliation across samples, and swanViewer/processSwan.py isoform and differential-expression exploration. The wet-lab half (cell culture and differentiation, ONT library construction, PromethION sequencing) is out of scope for computational reproduction.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from the Methods section (Culturing control and edited cell lines; Direct whole-genome long-read sequencing; Sequencing direct DNA libraries; Processing of Nanopore data; Differentially methylated site calling; Measuring methylation level of regions; Phasing genomic reads; Reconciling novel isoforms across different samples; Downstream analysis of RNA expression level and isoform usage using swanViewer). The Dogme pipeline is decomposed into its four named sub-invocations (basecalling, mapping, modification extraction, quantification) because the paper pins a separate version and separate parameters for each. UCSC track download plus bigBedToBed conversion is folded into the modkit dmr pair region-scoring step, since the tracks are the input bed for that single invocation. Wet-lab steps are recorded as layer W with verdict X: W = 4, S = 12.

steps.label: Culture of immortalized skeletal myoblast control cells and the DEL9_SM double-mutant line (high-glucose DMEM, 20% FBS, 1% Pen-Strep, 2% Ultrasor G) and differentiation to late myotube stage (2% FBS + 1% ITS, collected day 12 control / day 14 mutant); the mutant line was generated previously with Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 (Kong et al., iScience 2024)

Nanopore genomic DNA library construction: 1.4 ug labelled DNA per library, Ligation Sequencing Kit V14 (ONT SQK-LSK114), NEBNext Companion Module (NEB E7180), AMPure XP beads (Beckman A63881), Long Fragment Buffer washes, overnight 4 C elution, Qubit dsDNA HS quantification
Direct-RNA library construction for control and FSHD myotubes in biological duplicate (built by N.M. and E.T. per Author contributions; kit details only partially given in prose)

Sequencing on PromethION 2 Solo with PromethION R10.4.1 flow cells (ONT FLO-PRO114M), 400-450 ng per load, BSA-supplemented priming mix, MinKNOW v24.02.16 at 400 bps; average 60 Gb per genomic sample (min ~20x), average 10 M reads per direct-RNA replicate
Basecalling of pod5 files with dorado v1.0.0 inside the Dogme v1.2.2 nextflow pipeline (Dogme cited as ref 37; modified-base calling for 5mC/5hmC on DNA and for RNA)

Read mapping with minimap2 v2.28 and samtools v1.15.1 against both GRCh38 and CHM13 T2T assemblies; preset -ax lr:hq for genomic reads and -ax splice:hq for direct-RNA reads ('for the full list of parameters, see the package documentation')

Extraction of base modifications from BAM into bedMethyl with modkit v0.5.0; RNA modification probability threshold fixed at 0.9, genomic threshold set by modkit sampling 10,000 reads and discarding the lowest-confidence 10% of calls
Transcript quantification with LR-kallisto and bustools, stated as 'LR-Kallisto and bustools v0.51.1 and v0.43.2 respectively', run inside Dogme

Differentially methylated site calling with DSS (Dispersion Shrinkage for Sequencing data, ref 82) v2.50.1: bedMethyl filtered at min coverage 3 reads and per-sample max coverage at the 99th percentile, modifications split into separate inputs, bed files split by chromosome, DMLtest then callDMR, p-value threshold 0.05, per-chromosome TSVs concatenated

Construction of promoter regions from a GENCODE annotation file with an unnamed 'custom script': TSS from strand orientation and start position, 2000 bp upstream and 500 bp downstream, clipped to chromosome length, isoform promoters overlapping less than 50% kept separate; significance defined as a methylation difference exceeding two standard deviations

Region-level methylation scoring with the modkit dmr pair subcommand (v0.4.3) over RepeatMasker Repetitive Elements and single-read/multi-read Mappability tracks downloaded from the UCSC Genome Browser and converted BigBed to Bed with bigBedToBed; 'no change' defined as a mean methylation difference of 5% or less
Visualisation of methylation and read-level evidence with the Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV, ref 83)

Variant calling for phasing: all edited samples and isogenic controls merged into one BAM at ~100x coverage, Clair3 v1.1.1 (ref 84) with --platform="ont" --model_path=r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v500 --use_whatshap_for_final_output_phasing --enable_long_indel
Read phasing with WhatsHap v2.7 (ref 85) using default parameters; promoter regions with fewer than three phased reads excluded, removing eighteen transcripts from fifteen FSHD genes

Novel-isoform reconciliation across samples with reconcileBams.py (merging incomplete splice matches into representative transcripts, correcting strand assignment, retaining novel isoforms only if >0.1 TPM in 2 or more samples) producing a consensus GTF, tagged BAMs and a known+novel abundance file; script located at https://github.com/mortazavilab/dogme/tree/main/scripts

Downstream isoform and differential-expression analysis with the swanViewer Streamlit application (https://github.com/mortazavilab/swanViewer), preceded by processSwan.py which builds a SwanGraph (Swan, ref 86) from the reconciled GTF plus abundance matrices and serialises it with metadata to Python pickle files; README adds pyDESeq2 and Swan DIE analysis and a prebuilt image ghcr.io/mortazavilab/swanviewer/swan-app:latest

headline.static_readiness: 0/12 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 9/12 (75%) computational steps reach RI at stage 1 - unusually high version discipline for a mixed wet-lab/computational paper. Exact pins are given in prose for Dogme v1.2.2, dorado v1.0.0, minimap2 v2.28, samtools v1.15.1, modkit v0.5.0 (and v0.4.3 for the dmr pair step), bustools v0.51.1 / LR-kallisto v0.43.2, DSS v2.50.1, Clair3 v1.1.1 (with model r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v500) and WhatsHap v2.7, plus MinKNOW v24.02.16 on the wet-lab side. Three steps cap at NI: C6 (promoter construction by an unnamed custom script with no GENCODE release stated), C8 (IGV, no version, no session) and C12 (swanViewer has no release tag and its container is pulled by the floating :latest tag). The binding constraint is not code availability - Dogme and swanViewer are both live, MIT/licensed, actively maintained public repositories - but (a) environment closure, since Dogme ships no environment.yml, requirements.txt or lockfile and its container is likewise :latest, and (b) data access, since the raw ONT data is only 'being deposited' to controlled-access dbGaP phs002554. Even under the most generous inference-inclusive reading the paper cannot exceed RI at stage 1; a stage-2 read of the Dogme v1.2.2 release tree is what would decide whether the nextflow.config / dogme.profile / GHCR image constitutes validated environment capture.
headline.coverage: 12 computational steps and 4 wet-lab steps assessed from the full-text Methods section (Culturing control and edited cell lines through Downstream analysis ... using swanViewer), the Data availability statement, and the landing-page README prose of both linked GitHub repositories (mortazavilab/dogme, mortazavilab/swanViewer). Supplementary tables S1-S2 (DEG tables) were not fetched at stage 1. No code was read line-by-line.

gaps.where: Raw ONT genomic and direct-RNA data for every computational step (C1-C11)
gaps.missing: Data availability states verbatim: 'Data is being deposited in dbGaP study accession phs002554.' The present progressive means the deposit is not asserted as complete at posting time, and dbGaP is controlled access requiring a Data Access Request, so no reader can pull the pod5/BAM inputs without an approved application. Only the derived direct-RNA isoform dataset for swanViewer is openly available (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18022278). No accession is given for the previously published short-read data that the paper repeatedly compares against ('we revisited our short-read data').
gaps.how_to_close: Confirm the dbGaP deposit is released and state the release status, add the accession for the comparison short-read dataset, and deposit derived per-sample bedMethyl / abundance matrices openly so the downstream half (C5-C12) can be re-run without a controlled-access application.

gaps.where: Software environment across all 12 computational steps
gaps.missing: No lockfile, no resolved environment specification, and no digest-pinned container. The Dogme repository root contains dogme.nf, nextflow.config, dogme.profile, SingularityConfigExample.conf, modkitModule.nf, nanoporeModule.nf, scripts/ and testdata/ - there is no environment.yml, requirements.txt, conda-lock, pixi.lock or Dockerfile. The README instructs the user to 'first install dorado, minimap2, samtools, modkit, kallisto, and bustools, and the latest version of nextflow and add their paths to the dogme.profile', i.e. environment resolution is delegated to the host. The published images are referenced only by floating tag (ghcr.io/mortazavilab/dogme-pipeline:latest and ghcr.io/mortazavilab/swanviewer/swan-app:latest), never by sha256 digest. The DSS step additionally has no R version or R package closure, and swanViewer's README lists nine Python dependencies (streamlit, swan-vis, pyDESeq2, pandas, matplotlib, anndata, scanpy, numpy, plotly) with no version constraints at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a digest-pinned container (or conda-lock / pixi.lock) covering the ONT toolchain and the R/Python analysis side, tag the image per release rather than :latest, and record the R sessionInfo() used for DSS.

gaps.where: C5 (DSS), C6 (promoter construction), C7 (modkit dmr pair over UCSC tracks), C9 (BAM merge before Clair3)
gaps.missing: The study-specific glue is not released. The bedMethyl-to-DSS reformatting and per-chromosome splitting, the promoter-region 'custom script', the UCSC track download and bigBedToBed conversion, the two-standard-deviation and 5% significance rules, and the ~100x BAM merge are described in prose only; no repository, script name or notebook is cited for any of them. Only Dogme (pipeline) and swanViewer (viewer) are released, and neither is a paper-specific analysis repository.
gaps.how_to_close: Create a paper-specific analysis repository (or a Zenodo-archived scripts bundle) containing the DSS driver, the promoter-construction script, the modkit dmr pair invocations, the merge/filtering steps and the figure code, and cite it in a Code availability statement.

gaps.missing: The reconcileBams.py link resolves to the main branch (github.com/mortazavilab/dogme/tree/main/scripts), not to the v1.2.2 tag the Methods pins; the repository has since advanced (releases up to v1.3.2, last push 2026-07-07), so the file at the cited URL is not the file used. swanViewer carries no version, tag or release at all in the paper or the README, and its container is pulled by :latest.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite permalinks at the exact tag or commit SHA (github.com/mortazavilab/dogme/tree/v1.2.2/scripts), cut and cite a swanViewer release, and archive both to Zenodo with DOIs.

gaps.where: C1 (dorado), C2 (minimap2), C4 (LR-kallisto/bustools), C7 (modkit dmr pair), C8 (IGV)
gaps.missing: Parameters are deferred rather than stated. For mapping the paper says explicitly 'for the full list of parameters, see the package documentation', which points at a moving target rather than a recorded invocation. The dorado basecalling model is not named in the Methods (only the Clair3 model r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v500 is given, which implies but does not state the basecalling model). The kallisto index, its source annotation and the bustools workflow options are unstated. The modkit dmr pair flags are unstated. IGV has no version and no session/track configuration.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the resolved command lines actually executed (Dogme already ships scripts/software_versions.py which writes a per-run ${sample}.softwareVersion.txt - publishing that file per sample would close most of this gap), name the dorado model, and state the kallisto index provenance.

gaps.missing: The genomic modification-probability threshold is not a fixed number but is estimated by modkit from a random sample of 10,000 reads; no seed is stated, so the threshold - and therefore every downstream DMS call - is not bitwise reproducible. No seed is reported for any DSS step either.
gaps.how_to_close: State the sampling seed (or the resolved per-sample threshold values that modkit computed) and record seeds for any stochastic step.

gaps.missing: External reference resources are named but not versioned: 'GRCh38' and 'the CHM13 T2T assembly' with no patch level, source URL or accession; 'a gencode annotation file' with no release number; UCSC RepeatMasker Repetitive Elements and single-read/multi-read Mappability tracks with no track version or download date. ENCODE cCREs (ref 40) are used to note that only 13 of 63 DUX4 target genes have annotated promoters, again with no release identifier.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin each external resource by accession/release and download date (e.g. GCA_000001405.15 GRCh38.p14, CHM13v2.0, GENCODE vNN, UCSC track table name plus retrieval date) and archive the derived bed files alongside the analysis code.

gaps.where: Code availability statement (absent) and the DUX4 target gene list
gaps.missing: There is no Code availability section; the two repository URLs appear only inside Methods subsections. The set of 63 DUX4 target genes analysed throughout is attributed to prior ChIP-seq studies (cited as '32-34', a citation range that appears inconsistent with the surrounding numbering) but the gene list itself is not provided as a machine-readable file in the main text - it is reachable only through supplementary Table S1/S2.
gaps.how_to_close: Add an explicit Code availability statement listing all repositories with tags, and publish the 63-gene target list and the 2.5 kb promoter interval bed as supplementary data files.
